subject.title: feat(config): journal every config change with source labels and manual-edit detection

question: Should this phase guarantee complete coverage for all supported config write owners and invalid offline edits before landing, or should the feature claim and scope be narrowed to root-file writes only?
rationale: The branch presents universal mutation journaling as its user contract, but completing that contract crosses the public runtime write wrapper, include-owned mutation path, and pre-reloader startup validation boundary; maintainers need to choose the permanent scope rather than leave a partial promise implicit.

options.title: Complete universal coverage
options.body: Propagate origin through the runtime writer, journal include-owned mutations, and move invalid-offline observation before the startup abort path.

options.title: Narrow the phase contract
options.body: Limit this phase to root `openclaw.json` changes and revise the operator-facing claim plus follow-up scope so unsupported include and invalid-startup cases are not represented as covered.

recommendation.title: Complete universal coverage
recommendation.body: Propagate origin through the runtime writer, journal include-owned mutations, and move invalid-offline observation before the startup abort path.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked phase design and current implementation commits establish the clearest available ownership signal for deciding the intended contract.
